findings.evidence: `pkg/executor/hash_table.go:156` (`GetOneMatchedRow`): after `GetRowAndAppendToChunkIfInDisk` assigns `c.chkBuf`, a collision path does `capacity = c.chkBuf.Capacity()` (`pkg/executor/hash_table.go:185`) and later `c.chkBuf.Reset()` (`pkg/executor/hash_table.go:190`) with no nil guard. But `GetRowAndAppendToChunkIfInDisk` returns a nil chunk when not spilled (`pkg/util/chunk/row_container.go:288`, return `..., nil, nil` at `pkg/util/chunk/row_container.go:299`), so `c.chkBuf` becomes nil in the common non-spill case. This fast path is exercised for semi/anti/left-outer-semi joins without conditions via `pkg/executor/join.go:925` (call at `pkg/executor/join.go:931`).
findings.fix: In `GetOneMatchedRow`, only compute/reset capacity when `c.chkBuf != nil` (spilled case). For the non-spill case (`c.chkBuf == nil`), skip chunk-capacity bookkeeping entirely, and guard the modulo/reset branch to avoid divide-by-zero. Keep collision counting unchanged.
findings.impact: If a hash bucket contains entries that share the same 64-bit hash but have different join keys (a case the code explicitly handles via `matchJoinKey`/`probeCollision`), the first mismatching entry will trigger a nil-pointer panic in `GetOneMatchedRow`, aborting the join worker. TiDB recovers probe-worker panics into query errors, so this manifests as a query failure; in worst cases it can become a denial-of-service vector if collisions can be induced.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on upstream/master (`b75374faa6`): the same nil-unsafe pattern exists in `pkg/executor/join/hash_table_v1.go:146` (uses `c.chkBuf.Capacity()` at `pkg/executor/join/hash_table_v1.go:175`), and `upstream/master` `RowContainer.GetRowAndAppendToChunkIfInDisk` still returns a nil chunk when not spilled.
findings.verify: Add a unit test alongside `pkg/executor/hash_table_test.go` that forces collisions (similar to existing `hashCollision`) and calls `GetOneMatchedRow` in non-spill mode; assert it does not panic and returns a matching row (or nil if none). Also run existing hash-table collision tests to ensure `probeCollision` remains tracked.
findings.what: New `hashRowContainer.GetOneMatchedRow` can panic on hash collisions when the underlying `RowContainer` has not spilled, due to dereferencing `c.chkBuf` even when it is nil.

subject: executor: optimize (left outer) (anti) semi join which has no other condition (#47764)
summary: Adds a hash join fast path for (left outer) (anti) semi joins with no additional filter by probing only one matched build row (new `hashRowContainer.GetOneMatchedRow`) gated via `joiner.isSemiJoinWithoutCondition()`. Refactors `baseHashTable.Get` to return an entry chain pointer and updates CTE dedup + index lookup hash join to iterate the chain; also fixes `nullAwareAntiLeftOuterSemiJoiner.Clone` returning the wrong type.
